key_insight: Reuse previously generated off-policy trajectories by conditioning the policy on successful prefixes, turning old inference/RL FLOPs into useful supervision that boosts learning on hard problems where on-policy successes are rare.
problem_solved: Standard RL on difficult reasoning tasks wastes compute because correct on-policy traces are scarce, gradients vanish, and training stalls; the paper addresses how to reuse past off-policy computation safely and effectively to restart learning.
method: Condition the policy on prefixes of successful off-policy traces so the model continues from partially successful contexts instead of treating off-policy data as full-target supervision.
Integrate prefix-conditioning into the RL optimization pipeline to convert off-policy sampling FLOPs into actionable learning signals while avoiding typical off-policy instabilities.
Train/finetune the model to complete conditioned prefixes (and then use RL updates), enabling reuse of prior inference or training trajectories to improve sample and compute efficiency.
impact: Makes RL practical on hard LLM reasoning tasks by converting wasted inference/RL compute into reusable training signal, improving sample-efficiency and accelerating learning where conventional on-policy RL fails.
visual_elements: Schematic: model conditioned on a prefix (highlighted) of a trajectory and generating the continuation — shows prefix→completion flow.
Before/After bar chart: on-policy-only training vs. PrefixRL sample- or compute-efficiency (fewer FLOPs to reach a success rate).
Pipeline diagram: collect traces → extract successful prefixes → conditioned RL updates → improved policy, emphasizing FLOP reuse loop.
Icon set: clock/FLOP reuse, shield for stability (avoiding off-policy collapse), and a rising-learning curve for faster convergence.
paper_title: Reuse your FLOPs: Scaling RL on Hard Problems by Conditioning on Very Off-Policy Prefixes
paper_authors: Amrith Setlur, Zijian Wang, Andrew Cohen, Paria Rashidinejad, Sang Michael Xie
